alerts.headline: Flood Warning issued November 3 at 10:49AM EST by NWS Melbourne FL
alerts.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Cocoa 9w affecting Brevard County.

.Heavy rainfall has caused the St. Johns River near Cocoa to rise
into Minor Flood Stage. The river is forecast to climb into Moderate
Flood Stage in the next couple days, approaching Major Flood Stage
late in the week.

For the St. Johns River...including Cocoa...Moderate flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and moderate flooding is
forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Cocoa 9w.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 17.0 feet, Flooding to some roads and water
approaching low lying homes in the Silver Pines subdivision in
Rockledge. Many yards, ditches and pastures flooded and water
approaching low lying structures along Pluckebaum Road in Cocoa and
Rockledge. Flooding to low lying structures in the Lake Washington
area of Melbourne.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 10:15 AM EST Tuesday the stage was 16.4 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 15.8 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 10:15 AM EST Tuesday was 16.4 feet.
- Forecast...The river is forecast to climb into Moderate Flood

alerts.headline: Flood Warning issued November 3 at 9:30AM EST until November 4 at 9:30AM EST by NWS Melbourne FL
alerts.areas: Brevard, FL; Indian River, FL; Martin, FL; St. Lucie, FL
alerts.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is occurring.

* WHERE...Southeastern Brevard County in east central Florida...
Eastern Indian River County in east central Florida...
Northeastern Martin County in east central Florida...
St. Lucie County in east central Florida...

* WHEN...Until 930 AM EST Wednesday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying
and flood-prone locations is occurring. It will take several hours
for all the water from these storms to work through local drainage
systems in urban areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 925 AM EST, flooding continues across the warned area and
emergency management has reported numerous road closures across
portions of southern Brevard County and the Treasure Coast.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Port Saint Lucie, Palm Bay, Melbourne, Walton, Fort Pierce,
Sebastian, Stuart, Vero Beach, Fellsmere, Indian River Shores,
Malabar, Indialantic, Vero Beach South, Gifford, Winter Beach,
Indrio, Wabasso, Sebastian Highlands, Fort Pierce Inlet and
Roseland.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

advisories.agency: Brevard Public Schools (via Florida Today/Yahoo News)
advisories.text: Because of the extent of flooding across the county, all Brevard Public Schools campuses and district offices will stay closed Tuesday, Nov. 3. Schools are expected to reopen Wednesday.

advisories.agency: Brevard County Supervisor of Elections (via News 6)
advisories.text: Because of the historic flooding, some Election Day precinct polling locations are being moved temporarily for Tuesday's General Election. Voters should check where their precinct will vote before going.

advisories.agency: Brevard County Emergency Management (via Spectrum News 13)
advisories.text: Water on some roads has gone down since earlier in the day, but county officials still ask residents not to leave home unless they absolutely must or are under evacuation orders. The Red Cross has opened a shelter in Cocoa at Parker Memorial Missionary Baptist Church.

advisories.agency: Brevard County Sheriff's Office (via Space Coast Daily)
advisories.text: Sheriff Wayne Ivey says courts will be back in session Tuesday, Nov. 3, and many government offices are expected to reopen as flooding damage is assessed. Brevard Public Schools stay closed Tuesday so the district can inspect buildings. The full extent of flood damage is not yet known, so residents should stay off the roads unless they need to travel.

A water main break in Melbourne's system has cut water pressure, and in some cases all water service, for customers in Indialantic, Indian Harbour Beach, Melbourne Beach, Satellite Beach and some unincorporated areas that get their water from the City of Melbourne.

advisories.agency: City of Cocoa Beach (via News 6 WKMG)
advisories.text: Too much water is flowing into the Cocoa Beach wastewater treatment plant and lift stations. Residents, especially in the south end and Snug Harbor, are asked to limit nonessential water use.

Several roads and intersections in West Melbourne are still closed by flooding as of 8 a.m. Tuesday. Drive slowly and carefully, especially near flooded neighborhoods, because wakes from passing vehicles can push water into homes. Officials are still checking whether flooded areas are safe to travel.
Several Melbourne roads are still fully closed because floodwater has not drained. Many abandoned vehicles are still blocking roads and slowing emergency response.

advisories.agency: Brevard Public Schools (via Florida Today/Yahoo News)
advisories.text: Brevard Public Schools will stay closed for a third day in a row on Wednesday, Nov. 4. A district spokesperson said campus damage, flooded roads and water service outages mean the district can't open safely. District crews are continuing inspections, repairs and cleanup to get campuses ready to reopen.
